summary: This component renders a feedback widget that lets users vote on whether a blog article was helpful. It fetches vote counts from an API, stores the user's vote in localStorage to prevent duplicate voting, and displays a thank-you message with updated counts after they vote.

explanations.20: The permalink is cleaned by removing leading and trailing slashes, then converted to an empty string if it doesn't exist — this creates a unique identifier for each page.
explanations.28: The voted state starts as null instead of reading from localStorage immediately, because server-side rendering (which runs without localStorage) would differ from the client, causing React to complain about a mismatch.
explanations.36: This tries to read the user's previous vote from localStorage so we can show them they already voted; the try-catch prevents errors in private browsing modes where localStorage isn't available.
explanations.44: The component fetches the current vote counts by passing the page identifier to the API, using encodeURIComponent to safely handle any special characters in the slug.
explanations.45: This checks if the response was successful (r.ok) before trying to parse the JSON; if it failed, it returns null instead of throwing an error.
explanations.56: This sends the user's vote to the API as a POST request with both the page slug and their vote choice in the body.
explanations.69: After successfully voting, the vote is stored in localStorage so on the next visit we know this user already voted and can skip showing the buttons.
explanations.78: If there's no valid page identifier, the component returns null so nothing renders — this prevents the widget from appearing on pages where it shouldn't.
